summary.oneLiner: KM Sugar Mills is an integrated Indian sugar manufacturer evolving into a diversified enterprise through co-generation, distillery, and circular-economy by-product utilization.
summary.business: KM Sugar Mills manufactures sugar from sugarcane and operates an integrated business model that converts by-products into valuable resources. The company produces surplus power from bagasse-based co-generation sold to the state grid, and has a wholly-owned subsidiary, KM Spirits and Allied Industries Limited, incorporated to manufacture all types of spirits, though it is yet to commence operations. The company sells sugar primarily on cash terms, and ethanol and power to government undertakings.

endMarkets: India (domestic sugar market)|Uttar Pradesh state power grid|Government undertakings / oil manufacturing companies for ethanol

risks.risk: Promoter succession and board stability risk
risks.note: The sudden demise of founder promoter L.K. Jhunjhunwala (ceased 14.03.2026) and subsequent appointment of promoter-group member Naina Devi Jhunjhunwala as Additional Director (18.05.2026) introduces uncertainty in strategic supervision and family control dynamics.

risks.risk: Concentrated promoter-group control and related-party exposure
risks.note: Promoter and promoter group hold 56.51% of shares. Material related-party transactions continue, including Rs 2350 Lacs investment in OFCDs of K M Strategic Investments & Holding Pvt Ltd and a corporate guarantee of Rs 6174.21 lacs plus Rs 375 Lacs preference share investment in Sonar Castings Limited, creating potential conflict and capital-allocation risk.
Both the sugar unit and distillery unit are located in District Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh, exposing the company to region-specific agro-climatic, regulatory, and logistical disruptions.

As a sugar mill with a distillery unit, the company's performance is structurally tied to cane availability, government-set sugarcane pricing, sugar release mechanisms, and ethanol blending policies, which are outside management control.

The board includes an Independent, Executive Director-cum-CEO (S.C. Agarwal) responsible for strategic management and implementation, creating reliance on a single non-promoter executive for day-to-day leadership.

risks.risk: Limited board and committee independence in practice
risks.note: The Audit Committee includes one promoter executive director as member alongside two independent directors; the board has three promoter executive directors out of eight, and inter-se family relationships dominate the promoter bloc, potentially diluting independent oversight.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Sugar division crushed 111.63 Lacs quintals of cane, marginally higher than 110.98 lacs quintals in previous year, with average recovery of 10.90% (vs 11.01% prior year).
- Distillery produced 91.12 Lacs BL of Rectified Spirit and 90.58 Lacs BL of ethanol; ethanol sales volume increased to 88.33 Lacs BL from 72.39 Lacs BL in prior year.
- Country Liquor production declined to 13.79 Lacs cases from 16.27 Lacs cases, with sales at 13.68 Lacs cases vs 16.24 Lacs cases.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Demerger of Distillery Division into wholly owned subsidiary KM Spirits and Allied Industries Limited to create focused entities for sugar and distillery businesses, enabling independent growth strategies and access to capital markets.
- Continuous sugarcane development and agricultural mechanization to improve cane productivity, soil health, and farmer engagement through distribution of subsidized planters, promotion of trash mulching, scientific distance planting, and new variety trials.
- Energy conservation and efficiency improvement through equipment upgrades (rope couplings, helical gearboxes, VFDs, auto feed control valves) and utilization of bagasse-based cogeneration for captive power and surplus sale.
- No explicit dividend policy, buyback, or debt reduction philosophy stated in the provided governance sections. The report notes repayment of term loans and improved working capital, but no forward-looking capital allocation framework is disclosed.
- Company commitment to track prevalent corporate-governance practices and take affirmative steps for substantive compliance commensurate with its size, nature of business, and governing structure.
- Green initiative in corporate governance: paperless compliance and electronic delivery of notices/documents to shareholders' registered email addresses.
- Vigil mechanism/whistle-blower policy in place, overseen by Audit Committee, with stated protection against victimisation and direct access to Audit Committee chairman; no complaints received during the year.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company has a wholly owned subsidiary, KM Spirits and Allied Industries Limited, incorporated on 23-02-2018 to manufacture all types of spirits. The subsidiary is yet to commence operations. No other capacity expansion, capex projects, or commissioning timelines are disclosed in the provided annual-report text.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated business model diversifying into co-generation and distillation, utilizing by-products to mitigate commodity price cyclicality.
- Bagasse-based captive power generation reduces energy costs and provides surplus power sales to the state grid.
- Sugar sales are mostly on cash, and ethanol/power are sold to government entities, significantly mitigating credit default risk.
- Central government-fixed minimum sale price of sugar at Rs. 3,100 per quintal provides a floor to sugar realizations.

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Promoter succession and board stability risk — The sudden demise of founder promoter L.K. Jhunjhunwala (ceased 14.03.2026) and subsequent appointment of promoter-group member Naina Devi Jhunjhunwala as Additional Director (18.05.2026) introduces uncertainty in strategic supervision and family control dynamics.
- Concentrated promoter-group control and related-party exposure — Promoter and promoter group hold 56.51% of shares. Material related-party transactions continue, including Rs 2350 Lacs investment in OFCDs of K M Strategic Investments & Holding Pvt Ltd and a corporate guarantee of Rs 6174.21 lacs plus Rs 375 Lacs preference share investment in Sonar Castings Limited, creating potential conflict and capital-allocation risk.
- Single-location operational concentration — Both the sugar unit and distillery unit are located in District Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh, exposing the company to region-specific agro-climatic, regulatory, and logistical disruptions.
- Commodity-price and regulatory cycle dependency — As a sugar mill with a distillery unit, the company's performance is structurally tied to cane availability, government-set sugarcane pricing, sugar release mechanisms, and ethanol blending policies, which are outside management control.
- Key-person dependency in executive roles — The board includes an Independent, Executive Director-cum-CEO (S.C. Agarwal) responsible for strategic management and implementation, creating reliance on a single non-promoter executive for day-to-day leadership.
- Limited board and committee independence in practice — The Audit Committee includes one promoter executive director as member alongside two independent directors; the board has three promoter executive directors out of eight, and inter-se family relationships dominate the promoter bloc, potentially diluting independent oversight.
